system.description:
Network represents the geographical extent of a Setite's web of contacts, allies and retainers. Each dot expands the Setite's reach, though it does not by itself increase the number of people in the network — the player must still purchase dots of Allies, Contacts, Herd or Retainers, representing servitors readily at hand (usually in the Setite's home city). When the Setite arrives in another locale covered by his Network, a similar number of Allies, Contacts, Herd and Retainers become available there, becoming fully available at a rate of three dots per night (the player chooses the order). The Setite never permanently loses dots in those Backgrounds by moving about within his web of influence.

Without the Setite's physical presence, network members elsewhere can only serve as Contacts — gathering and relaying information — whether reached by message or through the Setite Sorcery power Whisper of the Sands.

System: One dot covers two distinct cities. Two dots cover three distinct cities. Three dots cover a small geographical region (such as the Nile Delta) or four distinct cities. Four dots cover a significant region (such as Upper Egypt or the Languedoc) or five distinct cities. Five dots cover a large geographic area (such as the Low Countries, France or Egypt) or six distinct cities. Larger settlements may have several agents; smaller ones typically have only one, at the Storyteller's discretion.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Three: Serpents
